## Reflection

I anchored on the dramatic high-dose signal in w_bac3cf3f1a at 20 uM — frac_mitotic_like z=+27.0 and tub_glcm_contrast z=+27.9 — and then let the mid-dose well w_6d94986897 at 0.6 uM decide the call: frac_large_nucleus z=+10.0 with an atlas match of Aurora kinase inhibitors 7/10 in e7. The review was correct that the 0.6 uM Aurora signal rested on 61 cells with only ~1 very large nucleus and no polyploidy, and e12 explicitly weakened it to mild enlargement with rare binucleation and candidates unknown. I downgraded Aurora from 0.68 to 0.52 but still submitted it, instead of promoting the cholesterol-lowering neighbours that were present in both e5 (2/10) and high-dose-only e6 (3/10).

Unblinded as simvastatin, an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor, the truth fits the weak, non-mitotic enlargement/low density better than a kinase arrest. I had retained cholesterol-lowering at 0.07-0.08 but never probed it because my acquisition plan spent the tiny budget on extremes and then requested describe_phenotype on fields that were never acquired.

- Flagged high-dose 20 uM frac_mitotic_like z=+27.0 as potentially generic mitotic toxicity rather than specific target engagement
- Hedged after e12 showed only mild enlargement without multinucleation or spindle defects, lowering Aurora from 0.68 to 0.52

What was wrong or missed:
- Over-weighted single-well e3 (61 cells, frac_large_nucleus z=+10.0) and its e7 Aurora 7/10 match despite that z-score reflecting ~1 cell and no polyploidy per review
- Under-weighted e5/e6 cholesterol-lowering signal and e4 microscopist call of microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers, with no mevalonate-rescue or lipid-phenotype test to discriminate statin from mitosis inhibitor
- Acquisition choice acquired only 2 wells (20 uM and 0.6 uM), so e8/e9 dose_response failed for lack of >=3 wells and left dose-dependence untested, then wasted a step requesting non-acquired fields f_24a8e5703be5 et al.
